sources.fact: LBBD77/DM Dagenham Heathway Mall is 2.79ha, publicly owned, minimum 500 and maximum 860 net dwellings, planning-permission-status not-permissioned.
The Brownfield record supplies POINT (0.148961 51.541183) with no polygon; point geometry is not the redevelopment red-line or legal title extent.
On 16 February 2026 Cabinet approved preparation of comprehensive development proposals for the Heathway Mall Shopping Centre and Millard Terrace and market testing of delivery solutions.
Cabinet approved a decant strategy using replacement social-rented homes at separate sites to enable Millard Terrace redevelopment.
The 2026 decision authorises work toward vacant possession and property acquisition; land assembly is not a planning consent.
Cabinet reconfirmed potential use of CPO powers if necessary, subject to further detailed reports before any CPO is made.
A future full business case is still required for capital funding and co-investment supporting comprehensive redevelopment.
The redevelopment issue is a key Cabinet decision with approved status; this governance approval is distinct from a planning application decision.
Issue chronology records publication, Cabinet consideration and call-in expiry in February 2026; it does not record a site-specific planning permission.
Cabinet on 16 June 2026 adopted the Dagenham Heathway SPD to guide regeneration and future development; SPD adoption is policy guidance, not permission.
LBBD states all Brownfield Register sites require planning permission.
The adopted Local Plan 2037 is the starting point for decisions but does not itself grant a site-specific consent.

examples.result: DM remains not-permissioned in the current Brownfield record despite 2026 Cabinet regeneration approvals.
500-860 is Brownfield/allocation capacity, not consented dwellings.
Decant approval is not a planning application decision.
Vacant-possession and acquisition authority do not prove an exact site/title polygon.
Potential CPO use is not treated as ownership completion or title transfer.
SPD adoption guides design/regeneration but does not create permission.
The DM Brownfield point is not buffered into a redevelopment boundary.
Promotion remains zero until an exact current planning case, exact title/site relation and current statutory overlays are verified.
